resolved.reason: Qualcomm’s fiscal 2026 earnings-call transcripts and Investor Day update support “dropped” because management stopped mentioning the standalone PC goal without reporting achievement or explicitly withdrawing it.

missing.what_was_said: Management said it remained on track to achieve its fiscal '29 long-term revenue commitment outlined at the 2024 Investor Day. This was a broad reaffirmation, not a restatement of the standalone $4 billion PC figure.

Management said its updated fiscal 2029 targets included more than $24 billion across Automotive and IoT plus more than $15 billion in Data Center, bringing the total non-handset revenue outlook to $40 billion, up from the previous $22 billion target. It did not identify a standalone PC revenue target.
Management said Qualcomm's fiscal 2029 targets were $40 billion in non-handset revenues, with over $15 billion from Data Center; this was a broad target, not a PC-specific revenue figure.

missing.what_was_said: Discussing HUMAIN, management said the engagement was progressing well and “we have started shipping,” with work on third-party workloads. It still expected fiscal 2027 to start showing revenue, distinguishing shipment progress from the revenue forecast.

Management expected both custom-chip engagements with global-scale hyperscalers to begin generating revenue in the December quarter. It had purchase orders and had already started wafers, materially advancing the earlier conditional customer discussions.

Custom accelerators began shipping in October, and AWS connectivity was expected to ramp later in November. Management guided to more than $650 million of data-center revenue in the December quarter, with growth through fiscal 2027 and a $7 billion annualized exit run rate. Those revenue figures were forecasts, not reported results.
